models.purpose: Predict 2028 medal counts from host status, athlete count, and past performance while treating zero as censored.
models.summary: A Tobit model predicts a latent count and censors it at zero. The error is split into noise and unobserved effects. MLE maximizes the split likelihood. The printed product index and the log-likelihood sum are watermark-split, so those two displays stay medium confidence.

governing_equations.label: censoring rule
governing_equations.source_expression: y = 0 if y* <= 0, and y = y* if y* > 0
governing_equations.purpose: Censor the latent count at zero.

governing_equations.label: latent regression
governing_equations.purpose: Linear predictor for the latent count.

governing_equations.label: variance split
governing_equations.purpose: Split error variance into noise and unobserved effects.

governing_equations.label: likelihood definition
governing_equations.purpose: Define the likelihood as the probability of the observed count.

governing_equations.label: censored and uncensored pieces
governing_equations.source_expression: P(y* <= 0) = Phi((-X_i beta)/sigma); P(y* = y_i) = phi((y_i - X_i beta)/sigma)
governing_equations.purpose: Split the likelihood at the censoring point.

governing_equations.label: log-likelihood
governing_equations.purpose: Take the log before numerical maximization.

governing_equations.label: t-statistic
governing_equations.purpose: Score a fitted coefficient.

equation_status.reason: The censoring rule, latent regression, variance split, likelihood, split densities, log-likelihood, and t-statistic are printed.

objectives: Maximize the likelihood of the observed medal counts.
constraints: A latent count at or below zero is observed as zero.

parameter_estimation.method: Maximum likelihood, numerical methods not named

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not stated. The later mixed model says MLE never quite converged.

assumptions: Host status, athlete count, and past performance can estimate performance.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Table 2 prints coefficients, t-statistics, and p-values. Figure 1 is named and was not read.

strengths: The censoring rule matches a medal count that cannot fall below zero.
limitations: The normal latent assumption is called restricting.
Maximizing this give us uses a plural subject with a singular verb.

models.section: 3.4.2 Mixed Linear Models and Hurdle Model
models.purpose: Predict medal counts inside clusters, with a hurdle only for the low-performing cluster.
models.summary: Clusters 0 and -1 use a mixed negative binomial. Cluster 1 uses a probit hurdle and then the same positive count. The prose says for Cluster -1 in one sentence and clusters 0 and -1 in the next. Both stay. Powell's method worked best. MLE never quite converged.

variables.normalized_name: medal count for country i in cluster j
variables.definition: medal count for country i in cluster j

governing_equations.label: negative binomial
governing_equations.source_expression: y_ij ~ NBinom(mu_ij, theta); mu_ij = exp(X_ij beta_j + Z_ij b_j)
governing_equations.purpose: Mixed negative-binomial mean for clusters 0 and -1.

governing_equations.label: probit
governing_equations.source_expression: P(Y_ij = 1 | X_ij, Z_ij) = Phi(X_ij beta_j + Z_ij b_j)
governing_equations.purpose: Probability of earning any medal in cluster 1.

governing_equations.label: link forms
governing_equations.source_expression: Phi^{-1}(P(Y_ij = 1)) = X_ij beta_j + Z_ij b_j; log(mu_ij) = X_ij beta_j + Z_ij b_j
governing_equations.purpose: Write both models as a linear predictor under a link.

governing_equations.label: hurdle prediction
governing_equations.source_expression: Predicted Number of Medals = (1 - P(Y_ij = 0)) * y_hat_ij
governing_equations.purpose: Combine the zero model and the positive count.

equation_status.reason: The negative binomial, probit, two link forms, and hurdle product are printed.

objectives: Account for cluster-level and country-level unobserved effects.
Account for zero medal counts in cluster 1.
constraints: Clusters 0 and -1 are treated as having a close to negligible chance of zero medals.

steps: Fit clusters 0 and -1 with the negative binomial.
Fit cluster 1 with a probit hurdle.
Multiply the positive count by the probability of earning a medal.
Weight predictors by variance after the first fit.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not stated. The prose says MLE never quite converged.

assumptions: The negative binomial is chosen because variance can exceed the meain.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Table 3 prints log-likelihood, AIC, and BIC. Zero-model cells for clusters 0 and -1 are dashes.

strengths: The hurdle separates a zero from a positive count.
Weighting cut AIC and BIC in half on page 10.
limitations: Page 23 says the same weighting did not help convergence.
Cluster -1 and clusters 0 and -1 are both printed.
missing_details: No athlete-count regression equation is printed.
Post-weight AIC and BIC numbers are not printed.

models.purpose: Find country-sport segments that may mark a great coach, then score their contribution.
models.summary: A four-Games window supplies the local mean and standard deviation. A rise of at least 2s is a positive change point. A fall of at most -3s is a negative change point. Segments with z-score at least 1.5 are kept. The coefficient of variation is computed and not used as a selection rule. Contribution and normalized contribution are printed. Table 16, Table 17, and Table 18 year columns are watermark-shifted.
